title: Google Scholar, Microsoft Academic, Scopus, Dimensions, Web of Science, and OpenCitations’ COCI: a multidisciplinary comparison of coverage via citations
extended_summary:
This paper does not match the requested 2025 secondary-school writing study. Instead, it is a bibliometrics study comparing the citation coverage of six scholarly data sources: Google Scholar, Microsoft Academic, Scopus, Dimensions, Web of Science, and OpenCitations’ COCI. The central question is how much overlap exists among these sources in the citations they identify to a large seed set of highly cited academic documents, and how this varies across disciplines.

The authors assembled a seed sample of 2,515 highly cited English-language documents published in 2006 and classified across 252 subject categories using Google Scholar Classic Papers. They then extracted citing documents from the six databases and matched records across sources using DOI matching and conservative title/author similarity rules. The study is not an educational intervention and includes no student or teacher participants; the units of analysis are citation records and scholarly databases.

Across 3,073,351 matched citation records, Google Scholar showed the broadest coverage, finding 88% of all citations and most citations found by the other databases. Microsoft Academic and Dimensions were generally stronger alternatives to Scopus and Web of Science in many fields, though with important disciplinary gaps, especially in some humanities areas and in parts of physics for Microsoft Academic. COCI had the smallest coverage because it depends on open reference deposits.

The authors conclude that Google Scholar remains the most comprehensive citation source overall, while Microsoft Academic and Dimensions can serve as useful alternatives to Scopus and Web of Science for many bibliometric purposes. They caution, however, that results depend on the highly cited English-language seed sample, conservative matching procedures, and rapidly changing database coverage over time.
quality_tier_rationale: The provided paper text is a bibliometric comparison of citation databases and does not evaluate any educational technology intervention, student writing support tool, or secondary-school writing outcome. It is peer-reviewed, but relative to the K-12 intervention-evidence framework, it provides no causal or descriptive evidence about an education intervention, so it falls outside the evidence scope for this extraction task.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational intervention impact on student writing or other learner outcomes is studied, so there is no applicable impact estimate.
